50	    targetIds.forEach((id, i) => { params[`t${i}`] = id; });
51	
52	    // The SQL cap is a HARDER ceiling than the top_k display budget: past it the
53	    // edges were never fetched, so raising top_k cannot reveal them and the trust
54	    // banner must not claim an exhaustive caller set. Fetch one extra row purely
55	    // to detect that we hit it.
56	    let edges;
57	    if (depth <= 1) {
58	      edges = db.all(
59	        `SELECT e.*, n.label AS from_label, n.type AS from_type, n.file_path AS from_file, n.start_line AS from_line
60	         FROM edges e JOIN nodes n ON n.id = e.from_id
61	         WHERE e.to_id IN (${placeholders}) AND e.relation IN (${EXECUTION_RELATIONS.map((relation) => `'${relation}'`).join(',')})
62	         LIMIT ${EDGE_FETCH_CAP + 1}`,
63	        params
64	      );
65	    } else {
66	      edges = db.all(
67	        `WITH RECURSIVE callers(from_id, to_id, depth) AS (
68	           SELECT from_id, to_id, 1
69	           FROM edges
70	           WHERE to_id IN (${placeholders}) AND relation IN (${EXECUTION_RELATIONS.map((relation) => `'${relation}'`).join(',')})
71	           UNION ALL
72	           SELECT e.from_id, e.to_id, c.depth + 1
73	           FROM edges e
74	           JOIN callers c ON e.to_id = c.from_id
75	           WHERE e.relation IN (${EXECUTION_RELATIONS.map((relation) => `'${relation}'`).join(',')}) AND c.depth < $depth AND c.depth <= 10
76	         )
77	         SELECT DISTINCT e.*, n.label AS from_label, n.type AS from_type, n.file_path AS from_file, n.start_line AS from_line, c.depth
78	         FROM callers c
79	         JOIN edges e
80	           ON e.from_id = c.from_id
81	          AND e.to_id = c.to_id
82	          AND e.relation IN (${EXECUTION_RELATIONS.map((relation) => `'${relation}'`).join(',')})
83	         JOIN nodes n ON n.id = e.from_id
84	         LIMIT ${EDGE_FETCH_CAP + 1}`,
85	        { ...params, depth }
86	      );
87	    }
88	
89	    const edgesTruncated = edges.length > EDGE_FETCH_CAP;
90	    if (edgesTruncated) edges = edges.slice(0, EDGE_FETCH_CAP);
91	
92	    // I1 / R2-2026-05-31 — an absence claim ("NO CALLERS") is the most dangerous
93	    // output. Graph-edge traversal can never honestly attest an EXHAUSTIVE
94	    // absence (it reads edges, not live per-symbol clangd evidence), so route
95	    // through buildAbsenceTrustLine — which ALWAYS emits the heuristic
96	    // non-exhaustive caveat pointing at code_intel_references — never a bare
97	    // "NO CALLERS" and never a "trustworthy/exhaustive absence".
98	    const absence = async (msg) => {
99	      // ⛔ READ THE DATABASE BEFORE THE FIRST AWAIT. This function is async and its callers `return`
100	      // its promise, so the enclosing `finally { db.close() }` runs while that promise is still
101	      // pending — any db access AFTER an await here fails with "The database connection is not
102	      // open". Placed after the await, the scope note threw on every call and its catch returned
103	      // '', so the feature was inert and the output looked exactly as it had before.
104	      const scope = unsearchedRelationNote({
105	        db, column: 'to_id', placeholders, params, symbol,
106	        searched: EXECUTION_RELATIONS, unsearched: UNSEARCHED_RELATIONS,
107	        // ⚠ graph_impact, NOT graph_preflight: the default tool profile does not list preflight,
108	        // and the repo's remedy-reachability guard rejects pointing a reader at an uncallable verb.
109	        remedy: 'graph_impact answers "who touches this" across the wider family.',
110	      });
111	      let line = '';
112	      // The language comes from the resolved target, so the construct-coverage clause appears on a
113	      // C/C++ absence and costs zero bytes anywhere else.
114	      try { line = '\n' + await buildAbsenceTrustLine({ noun: 'callers', db, repoRoot, freshness, language: targets[0]?.language }); }
115	      // ⛔ NOT an empty catch. Measured 2026-09-02: swallowing this shipped a BARE absence with no
116	      // TRUST, no SCOPE and no NOT MODELLED — indistinguishable from an authoritative "nothing calls
117	      // this". The answer still returns; the agent is told the caveat is missing.
118	      catch { line = '\n' + ABSENCE_TRUST_UNAVAILABLE; }
119	      // ⚠ The scope note goes WITH the absence claim, where the reader is deciding whether nothing
120	      // uses this symbol — not into a separate field they would have to know to consult.
121	      return prefixReadWarnings(msg + line + scope, freshness.warnings);
122	    };
123	
124	    if (edges.length === 0) return absence(`NO CALLERS for "${symbol}"${indexedScopePhrase(db)}. Try graph_whereis(symbol="${symbol}", expand=true) for an overview.`);
125	
126	    // NOTE (P0-4): `source_file`/`source_line` here carry the CALLER's
127	    // DECLARATION location, not the call site. That is deliberate — edges are
128	    // function-granular (see docs/known-limitations.md), so one edge can stand
129	    // for several call sites inside the caller and there is no single call-site
130	    // line to show. It is also what makes the `file` directory filter below mean
131	    // "callers living under this path". The location is honest data; what was
132	    // NOT honest was rendering it in a format that reads as a call site, so the
133	    // output now says which it is (see LOCATIONS note below).
134	    let mapped = edges.map(e => ({
135	      from_id: e.from_id, to_id: e.to_id, relation: e.relation,
136	      source_file: e.from_file, source_line: e.from_line,
137	      confidence: e.confidence,
138	      provenance: e.provenance ?? 'EXTRACTED',
139	      depth: e.depth ?? 1,
140	      from_type: e.from_type, fan_in: 1,
141	      from_label: e.from_label,
142	      to_label: symbol,
143	    }));
144	    if (rolledUp) mapped = collapseCallerEdges(mapped, symbol);

content.text:
Fixed. `graph_callers` was applying the directory filter after the SQL fetch had already been capped at 100 edges.

**Cause:** in `mcp/stdio/query/verbs/callers.js`, the edge query uses `LIMIT EDGE_FETCH_CAP + 1` with no `ORDER BY`. The `file` filter ran afterwards in JS. In your repro, about 120 heuristic callers outside the directory can fill the 100-row cap and push out the one `LSP_VERIFIED` caller. The filter then ran on a set that no longer contained it, so the verb answered `NO CALLERS from "<dir>"`.

**Fix:** the filter is now a SQL predicate on the caller's file path, in both the depth-1 and recursive queries. It matches the same prefix as the old JS `startsWith`, so the cap now applies only to callers inside the directory. The JS filter is still there but no longer changes anything.

**Test:** I added one test to `tests/unit/query/truncation-honesty.test.js`. It builds 120 `CALLS` edges from `noisy/` and one `LSP_VERIFIED` caller in `quiet/`, then queries with `file: 'quiet/'`.
- With the fix stashed, the test fails.
- With the fix, the file's 5 tests pass.
- `verbs.test.js`, `m1-caller-sets-do-not-merge.test.js` and `m1-cpp-caller-sets.test.js` also pass (31 tests).
- I did not run the whole suite.
- I tested the depth-1 path only; the `depth>1` query got the same predicate but has no test.

Not committed yet.
